body:
Geographical location

Gujarat occupies the westernmost part of India. Its geographical position provides access to the Arabian Sea, an international land boundary with Pakistan and important land connections with northern, central and western India.

The state was formed on 1 May 1960 following the division of the former Bombay State into Gujarat and Maharashtra. Gujarat covers an area of approximately 196,024 square kilometres. Gandhinagar is its capital.

The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) passes through Gujarat. Consequently, parts of the state lie within the tropical zone, while areas north of this latitude lie outside it. Gujarat nevertheless experiences a predominantly tropical monsoon climate.

Political and geographical boundaries

DirectionNeighbouring area
North-westPakistan
North and north-eastRajasthan
EastMadhya Pradesh
South and south-eastMaharashtra
West and south-westArabian Sea

Gujarat also shares boundaries with parts of the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Diu lies near the southern coast of Saurashtra, Daman lies along the southern Gujarat coast near Valsad, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli lies inland near the Gujarat–Maharashtra boundary.

Daman, Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli are not districts of Gujarat. They belong to a separate Union Territory.

The basic shape of Gujarat

Three large geographical units help establish the state's map orientation:

  • Kachchh: The north-western region, containing the Great Rann, the Little Rann along its south-eastern side and extensive dry uplands.
  • Saurashtra: The peninsula lying between the Gulf of Kachchh and the Gulf of Khambhat.
  • Mainland Gujarat: The eastern portion of the state, extending from the northern plains towards the southern coastal plains and eastern hills.

The Gulf of Kachchh separates much of Kachchh from northern Saurashtra. The Gulf of Khambhat separates eastern Saurashtra from the central and southern Gujarat mainland.

Coastline length

Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states. Its indented coast, gulfs, creeks, tidal flats and islands create favourable conditions for ports, fisheries, salt production and coastal industries.

The official coastline measurement was revised in 2025 using improved geographical data and high-resolution mapping of the high-water line.

MeasurementGujarat coastline
Previous central government measurement1,214.70 km
Revised official measurement, 20252,340.62 km

The revised measurement was promulgated through a central government circular dated 29 April 2025 and reported in a parliamentary answer on 4 December 2025. Older geographical publications also commonly describe Gujarat's coastline as approximately 1,600 km. These figures reflect different measurement conventions and should not be treated as interchangeable.

The revised coastline length does not mean that Gujarat physically acquired more than 1,000 km of new coastline. More detailed measurement captures geographical irregularities that were previously omitted.

Reading a Gujarat map correctly

A political map identifies districts, settlements and administrative boundaries. A physical map identifies relief features such as hills, plains, rivers and coastal landforms. A thematic map represents a particular subject, such as rainfall, industries, wildlife or earthquake susceptibility.

Direction, scale and symbols are the three basic components of a map. The north indicator establishes orientation, the scale relates map distance to ground distance, and the legend explains the symbols used. These components must be interpreted before comparing geographical locations.

Prelims focus

  • Gujarat was formed on 1 May 1960.
  • Gandhinagar is the state capital.
  • The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat.
  • Saurashtra lies between the Gulf of Kachchh and the Gulf of Khambhat.
  • The revised official Gujarat coastline measurement is 2,340.62 km, promulgated in 2025.
  • Trap: Gujarat has the longest coastline among states, not among all states and Union Territories combined.

[Sources: NCERT, Class 6, The Earth: Our Habitat, 2018–19 edition, Chapter 4, Maps, pp. 24–29; Survey of India, Gujarat State Map, English, 1st edition, 2026; Ministry of Earth Sciences, Parliament Question: Coastline of the Country, 4 December 2025; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]

title: Gujarat: Location, Boundaries and Map Orientation

body:
Administrative divisions

A district is an administrative territorial unit within a state. District boundaries are established for governance and may change when new districts are created. A district headquarters is the principal administrative centre of that district.

Gujarat had 33 districts before the creation of Vav-Tharad. On 2 October 2025, Vav-Tharad was separated from Banaskantha and became the state's 34th district. Its headquarters is Tharad. The headquarters of Banaskantha remains Palanpur.

The district administration identifies Vav-Tharad as a northern district situated east of the Rann of Kachchh and south of Rajasthan. It comprises 8 talukas: Vav, Tharad, Suigam, Lakhani, Deodar, Bhabhar, Rah and Dharnidhar.

As of 26 November 2026, Gujarat has 34 districts according to the official district administration's record of the creation of Vav-Tharad.

Regional grouping of districts

For geographical study, the districts may be grouped into Kachchh, Saurashtra, North Gujarat, Central Gujarat and South Gujarat. These are convenient regional groupings rather than a single statutory system of administrative divisions. Different departments may group districts differently for their administrative purposes.

Kachchh and Saurashtra

DistrictHeadquarters
KachchhBhuj
JamnagarJamnagar
Devbhumi DwarkaKhambhalia
PorbandarPorbandar
JunagadhJunagadh
Gir SomnathVeraval
AmreliAmreli
BhavnagarBhavnagar
BotadBotad
RajkotRajkot
MorbiMorbi
SurendranagarSurendranagar

Kachchh occupies the north-western part of the state and is Gujarat's largest district by area. The Saurashtra districts form the western peninsular region and its adjoining interior.

North Gujarat

DistrictHeadquarters
Vav-TharadTharad
BanaskanthaPalanpur
PatanPatan
MehsanaMehsana
SabarkanthaHimmatnagar
AravalliModasa

North Gujarat includes extensive dry plains and the north-eastern hill tracts. The districts near Rajasthan experience relatively low rainfall compared with southern Gujarat.

Central Gujarat

DistrictHeadquarters
GandhinagarGandhinagar
AhmedabadAhmedabad
KhedaNadiad
AnandAnand
MahisagarLunawada
PanchmahalGodhra
DahodDahod
VadodaraVadodara
Chhota UdepurChhota Udepur

Central Gujarat contains major river valleys, fertile agricultural plains, industrial cities and eastern uplands. Gandhinagar may also be grouped with North Gujarat in some regional classifications.

South Gujarat

DistrictHeadquarters
BharuchBharuch
NarmadaRajpipla
SuratSurat
TapiVyara
NavsariNavsari
ValsadValsad
DangAhwa

South Gujarat extends from the lower Narmada valley towards Maharashtra. Its western part contains fertile coastal plains, while its eastern and south-eastern areas include forested hills.

District map and spatial relationships

Gandhinagar lies north of Ahmedabad. Vadodara lies south-east of Ahmedabad, Bharuch lies farther south along the Narmada, and Surat lies south of Bharuch along the Tapi. Navsari and Valsad continue this general southward sequence.

In Saurashtra, Jamnagar lies on the northern side of the peninsula, Porbandar on its western coast, Junagadh in the south-western interior, Gir Somnath along the southern coast and Bhavnagar on the eastern side near the Gulf of Khambhat. Rajkot occupies an interior position.

Older district maps require particular care. A place shown within a larger parent district on an old map may belong to a newly created district on a more recent map.

The Survey of India's 2026 Gujarat State Map notes that the newly formed Vav-Tharad district boundary is yet to be verified by state government authorities. Its district status and headquarters are established, but the precise mapped boundary in that edition carries this qualification.

Prelims focus

  • Vav-Tharad became Gujarat's 34th district on 2 October 2025.
  • Vav-Tharad was carved out of Banaskantha.
  • Devbhumi Dwarka has its headquarters at Khambhalia.
  • Kheda has its headquarters at Nadiad; Mahisagar at Lunawada.
  • Narmada has its headquarters at Rajpipla; Tapi at Vyara; Dang at Ahwa.
  • Trap: A district headquarters is not necessarily a town bearing the same name as the district.

[Sources: Survey of India, Gujarat State Map, English, 1st edition, 2026, district headquarters and administrative boundary legend; Government of Gujarat, Vav-Tharad District, About District and History; Central Ground Water Board, Summary on Status of Dynamic Ground Water Resources of Gujarat as on 2023, district and taluka directory, issued 2024; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]
title: Districts, Headquarters and Regional Divisions of Gujarat

body:
Physiographic classification

Physiography describes the physical character of the Earth's surface, including its plains, plateaus, hills, mountains and coastal features. Gujarat contains considerable variation in relief despite its relatively extensive lowlands.

Gujarat can be divided into 5 broad physiographic zones based on its relief and geological characteristics.

Physiographic zonePrincipal characteristics
Alluvial plainsExtensive river-deposited plains of mainland Gujarat
Eastern hilly tractHills extending from north-eastern Gujarat towards Dang
Saurashtra and Kachchh uplandsRocky uplands, hills and plateaus
Coastal alluvial plainsLow-lying coastal land and river-mouth deposits
Rann of KachchhExtensive saline and marshy lowlands

Kachchh and the Rann

Kachchh consists of rocky uplands surrounded by extensive low-lying saline areas. It contains both hilly terrain and flat salt-covered landscapes.

Great Rann of Kachchh

The Great Rann lies predominantly north of the Kachchh uplands. It is a vast seasonal saline marsh. During the monsoon, rainfall and inflowing water inundate extensive areas. During the dry season, evaporation leaves salt deposits on the surface.

Little Rann of Kachchh

The Little Rann lies towards the south-east of the main Kachchh uplands. It is also a seasonal saline wetland and is especially important as the habitat of the Indian wild ass.

Banni grasslands

The Banni grasslands lie along the southern margin of the Great Rann, north of the principal Kachchh uplands. They are dry grassland ecosystems supporting pastoral livelihoods and wildlife. They are distinct from the extensive salt-encrusted flats of the Rann.

The Rann is not simply a sandy desert. Its characteristic features are seasonal inundation, saline soils and extensive salt flats.

Saurashtra uplands

Saurashtra consists largely of rocky uplands and rolling plains, surrounded by coastal lowlands. Much of the peninsula is associated with the basaltic rocks of the Deccan Trap.

Its important hills include the Girnar, Barda and Gir hill systems. Rivers originating in the interior uplands flow towards different parts of the surrounding coast. This outward drainage arrangement is commonly described as radial drainage.

  • Girnar: Located near Junagadh; it contains Gujarat's highest mountain summit.
  • Barda Hills: Located in western Saurashtra near Porbandar and Devbhumi Dwarka.
  • Gir Hills: Located in southern Saurashtra and associated with the Gir forest ecosystem.
  • Chotila: An isolated prominent hill in Surendranagar district.
  • Shatrunjaya Hills: Located near Palitana in Bhavnagar district.

Eastern hill belt

The eastern hill belt forms a generally discontinuous upland region along Gujarat's eastern boundary. It includes extensions of major mountain systems of western and central India.

Hill systemLocation in Gujarat
AravalliNorth-eastern Gujarat, particularly Banaskantha, Sabarkantha and Aravalli
Vindhyan hill extensionsEastern and central-eastern Gujarat
Satpura hill extensionsSouthern side of the Narmada valley and eastern Gujarat
Western Ghats hill tractsExtreme south-eastern Gujarat, especially Dang

Saputara, a hill station in Dang district, lies in the northern extensions of the Western Ghats. The southern and south-eastern hills receive relatively high monsoon rainfall and support extensive forest vegetation.

Distinctive lowland regions

Several local geographical names identify particular lowlands within Gujarat. Their locations are useful for distinguishing regional map features.

RegionLocation and character
BhalFlat lowland near the northern and north-western margins of the Gulf of Khambhat
NalkanthaLowland surrounding Nal Sarovar, between mainland Gujarat and Saurashtra
GhedLow-lying coastal plain of western Saurashtra, particularly around Porbandar and Junagadh
BanniGrasslands between the Kachchh uplands and the Great Rann

The Ghed region is particularly susceptible to seasonal waterlogging because its low relief restricts drainage. The Bhal region contains extensive flat agricultural lands, while Nalkantha is closely associated with the Nal Sarovar wetland.

Prelims focus

  • The Great Rann lies north of the principal Kachchh uplands; the Little Rann lies towards their south-east.
  • Banni is a grassland region of Kachchh.
  • Girnar is located near Junagadh.
  • Saputara is located in Dang district and belongs to the Western Ghats hill region.
  • Bhal is associated with the Gulf of Khambhat; Nalkantha with Nal Sarovar; Ghed with western Saurashtra.
  • Trap: Girnar, Gir Hills and the Great Rann are distinct geographical features.

[Sources: Central Ground Water Board and Gujarat Water Resources Development Corporation, Report on Dynamic Ground Water Resources of Gujarat State as on March 2022, Sections 1.2–1.3, pp. 2–3; Central Ground Water Board, Gujarat Ground Water Resources Assessment, 2024 base year, Section 3.1, Physiography; Central Ground Water Board, Junagadh District Ground Water report, physiography section; Survey of India, Gujarat State Map, 2026; online sources consulted 26 November 2026.]
